entry.summary: Visa-free short stays as part of the Schengen area.
entry.max_stay: 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen area
entry.pre_arrival: None today. ETIAS is on the watch list.
entry.other: If you can't leave before the visa-free limit, go to the local questura (immigration office) before it runs out. Schengen Entry/Exit System: fingerprints and photo at the border on first entry (free, nothing to do beforehand). Get an entry stamp where one is still given, and carry your passport across internal borders.

tourism.detail: Australians may enter for tourism for up to 90 days in any 180-day period, subject to the shared Schengen count and border conditions.
tourism.next: Carry the passport, accommodation, funds and onward plan and check the rolling Schengen total.
tourism.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

meetings.detail: Official business guidance covers meetings, contacts, negotiations, industrial cooperation, company visits and related commercial activity.
meetings.next: Carry the Italian invitation stating the purpose and duration, and stop at negotiation rather than delivering the resulting service.
meetings.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

conference.route: Visa-free business or invitation purpose for attendance
conference.detail: Attending a fair, exhibition, congress or invited event can use the short-stay front door. Joining the program as a speaker or trainer is a separate professional activity.
conference.next: Carry registration and invitation; reclassify any panel, lecture, workshop or paid duty before travel.
conference.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

unpaid-speaking.route: Host and consulate classification before departure
unpaid-speaking.detail: The visa waiver includes invitations but official pages do not publish a broad exemption for a foreign professional merely because a talk is unpaid. A genuine cultural invitation may differ from professional service delivery, and expenses or other benefits should be disclosed.
unpaid-speaking.next: Ask the Italian host and the competent consulate to confirm in writing whether the exact appearance remains an invitation visit or needs a work or self-employment visa.
unpaid-speaking.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

paid-speaking.route: Short-stay self-employment visa where the category fits; salaried work or entertainment visa where the contract requires it
paid-speaking.detail: Official consular guidance says visa-exempt nationals still need a Schengen self-employment visa to exercise their profession. Italy's quota and out-of-quota categories are specific, so a general paid keynote should not be assumed to fit without classification.
paid-speaking.next: Give the consulate the contract, fee, professional category, host, venue and dates and obtain the correct visa before travel.
paid-speaking.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

book-launch.route: Visa-free business meetings plus a separately classified appearance
book-launch.detail: Publisher, agent and rights meetings fit the business lane. A public reading, workshop, appearance fee, direct retail and imported stock each add different professional, tax or customs questions.
book-launch.next: Use an Italian publisher or bookseller for local stock and receipts, and have the host classify the reading or launch before announcement.
book-launch.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

ai-teaching.route: University-professor or lecturer category where eligible; otherwise self-employment or salaried work
ai-teaching.detail: Official self-employment material lists university professors and certain lecturers among out-of-quota categories. A conference session, guest academic task and continuing corporate course should not be treated as the same route.
ai-teaching.next: Have the institution identify its legal category and provide the invitation or contract and required labour or police clearances.
ai-teaching.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

remote-work.route: Digital Nomad or Remote Worker visa
remote-work.detail: The route is for highly qualified remote activity: self-employed digital nomads use technology to work independently, while remote workers may work for an employer or client in Italy or abroad. Published requirements include qualifying education or experience, at least six months' prior experience, annual income of at least three times €8,500, accommodation and health insurance. Even a visa-exempt national is told to obtain this visa for a stay of 90 days or less.
remote-work.next: Use the Sydney consular checklist, prove the qualification and income route, and allow for the residence-permit step within eight working days of entry.
remote-work.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

entrepreneur.route: Italia Startup Visa or a qualifying self-employment entrepreneur route
entrepreneur.detail: An innovative startup route uses committee clearance and at least €50,000 dedicated funding. The current quota entrepreneur category requires an Italian-economy project with at least €500,000 investment and three new jobs; ownership does not replace personal work permission.
entrepreneur.next: Choose innovative startup, quota entrepreneur or another self-employment category before building the company and visa packet.
entrepreneur.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

trade.route: Visa-free business entry for fairs, negotiations and contracts; work and commercial setup for delivery
trade.detail: Trade fairs, factory visits, negotiations and equipment verification are published business purposes. Hands-on installation, professional training, local retail and operating an Italian business need closer classification.
trade.next: Use the first trip for partners and contracts, then map importer, seller, service provider, tax and work responsibility.
trade.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

artist.route: Short-stay self-employment or salaried entertainment visa
artist.detail: Short self-employed entertainment visas can sit outside quotas, but the published artist category is limited to renowned or highly qualified artists or recognised institutions and requires a contract. Salaried entertainment uses its own employment process.
artist.next: Have the Italian promoter choose employed or self-employed entertainment and confirm the artist threshold, contract and clearances.
artist.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

mixed-mission.route: Visa-free attendance and business elements plus separate permission for each professional element
mixed-mission.detail: Italy's visitor purposes are broad enough for scouting, invitations and negotiation but not a substitute for professional-work classification. Speaking, teaching, remote work, performance and direct sales each retain their own route.
mixed-mission.next: Send one complete schedule to the principal host and competent consulate and secure every required visa or clearance before departure.
mixed-mission.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

filming.route: Visa-free Schengen short stay (journalistic or media purposes)
filming.detail: Journalistic or media purposes are listed among visa-free purposes; paid production work and location permits are national matters.
filming.next: Ask the Embassy of Italy, Deakin about filming, and the local authority about locations.

research.route: Visa-free Schengen short stay (short-term study or training)
research.detail: Short-term study and training are covered; paid research at an institution is paid activity.
research.next: Ask the Embassy of Italy, Deakin if the host pays you.

volunteering.route: Volunteering D visa, authorised European programmes only
volunteering.detail: The volunteering D visa is limited to European Solidarity Corps and similar programmes authorised by the national youth agency; the national quota has issued no clearances since 2015.
volunteering.next: Treat independent volunteering as not available.

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The official currency of Italy is the euro (EUR). You must declare amounts over 10,000 euro or equivalent if you're travelling between Italy and any non-European Union (EU) country, including all forms of currency, not just cash. visa-preparation.fastest_entry: Visa-free short stays (90 days or less) as part of the Schengen area, in some cases.
visa-preparation.before_departure: Nothing to lodge before travel today: EES registration happens at the border. ETIAS hadn't started on 2026-11-01.
steps: Italy is in the Schengen area: short stays of 90 days or less can be visa-free in some cases; other purposes or longer stays need a visa before travel.
At the first Schengen border, give fingerprints and a photo for the Entry/Exit System (EES). It's free; nothing is needed before arrival, and sites charging for it are fraudulent.
Carry your passport when crossing borders, including inside Schengen (temporary internal checks are in place in places).
If you can't leave before the visa-free limit, contact the local questura; report wrong EES records at the next external border.

baseline_unverified.host_unlock: An Italian organiser, publisher, university or promoter can supply the invitation or contract and obtain or support the category-specific clearances for self-employment, salaried employment, entertainment or academic activity.
baseline_unverified.before_departure: Separate passive attendance and meetings from every programmed appearance. Send the Italian host and the competent consulate a schedule showing duties, payment, expenses, venue, audience and contract type.
baseline_unverified.useful_stay: The visa-free Schengen ceiling is 90 days in 180. Digital-nomad and remote-worker visas may be valid for up to 365 days and require a residence-permit application within eight working days of arrival.
baseline_unverified.from: Luke's earlier precursor notes; not verified against an official source and not an authority. Kept because no official page covers this point yet.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: No national etiquette guidance found on Italia.it, which covers practical travel only. Major churches set their own dress codes, typically covering shoulders and knees, with no hats; see the Vatican (va) and Milan Duomo (it/lombardy) records. There's no national tourist dress law. St Peter's Basilica bans shorts, bare shoulders, miniskirts and hats, and the Pantheon asks for appropriate clothing. Some cities fine conduct: Florence fines entering fountains (EUR 80 to 500).
culture-and-protocol.cultural_authority: Each church or site's own authority.
culture-and-protocol.note: No national government etiquette page; site rules apply.

drone-pilot-pathway.summary: EU baseline (EASA): register once as an operator in the state of residence or establishment, recognised across EASA states; Specific-category work in another state needs cross-border acceptance by that state's authority. National register, zone map and visitor rules checked 6 Nov 2026 (see items); footage routes not yet checked.

items.text: Not yet checked: whether the national aviation authority publishes a list of authorised operators.

EU rules (Regulations 2019/947 and 2019/945): operators register in the EASA state where they reside or are established; Specific-category operations need an operational authorisation or a standard-scenario declaration.

An operator registered in another EASA state may fly here; for Specific-category work it first gets the authorisation or STS declaration at home, then the destination authority must confirm the cross-border operation before flying. Rules for operators from outside EASA states: not yet checked.
Not yet checked: national tourism board or film commission media libraries.

ENAC says EU residents register with the aviation authority of their own country, and the registration is valid across the EU and Switzerland. Operators living outside the EU, including the UK, register in the first EU country they expect to visit. ENAC runs its registration through the d-flight portal.

For Specific-category work in Italy, an EU operator with an operational authorisation applies to ENAC at least 60 days ahead. The foreign operator also registers on d-flight to carry out the operation; that number is valid only for the confirmation and is not a national registration.

The d-flight portal shows the geographical zones, and ENAC says to check allowed and prohibited zones there. ENAC notes the zones come from the Italian AIP (aeronautical information publication), are approximated as simple shapes, and are under review. In some zones the zone authority's clearance (nulla osta) is also needed, in the Specific category and for some zones in the Open category.

ENIT's Open Library holds images released under Creative Commons licences, set per file (some are non-commercial or no-derivatives; filters exist for both). Video and aerial holdings, registration and who may use it were not confirmed.
